mainEntity.name: How much does a Mercedes-Benz A-Class 160 CDI engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A replacement engine for an A160 CDI typically costs between £350 and £3,800 depending on the engine code and condition. Used OM668 units start from £350-£800, reconditioned from £800-£1,600, and fully rebuilt OM607 engines from £2,200-£3,800. Labour for supply & fit adds £400-£800.

mainEntity.name: Does the Mercedes-Benz A-Class 160 CDI have a timing belt or timing chain?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the engine. The OM668 (W168, 1998-2004) and OM640 (W169, 2004-2012) use timing chains designed to last the lifetime of the engine. The OM607 (W176 facelift, 2013-2015) is a Renault-sourced engine with a timing belt that must be replaced every 80,000-100,000 miles. Enter your registration above to confirm which engine is fitted to your car.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of timing chain wear in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class 160 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: On OM668 and OM640 engines (W168 and W169), the most common symptom is a rattling noise from the engine on cold start. Other signs include poor performance, increased fuel consumption, and the engine management light illuminating. If you hear any unusual sounds, have the timing system inspected immediately.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes-Benz A-Class 160 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the generation and condition. A W168 A160 CDI is typically worth £800-£2,500 - a full engine replacement often exceeds the car's value, making a used engine or targeted repair more economical. A W169 A160 CDI is worth £1,500-£4,000 - a rebuilt OM640 engine (£1,500-£2,800) can be a worthwhile investment if the car is in good condition. A W176 A160 CDI is worth £4,000-£8,000 - a rebuilt OM607 engine is usually within the car's value.

mainEntity.name: What causes the Mercedes-Benz A-Class 160 CDI to lose power?

acceptedAnswer.text: Power loss in the A160 CDI can be caused by several issues depending on the engine. On OM668 and OM640 engines, timing chain wear can cause cam timing drift, reducing power. Clogged fuel injectors can lead to poor engine performance. On OM607 engines, a failing timing belt can cause timing drift. A diagnostic check with Mercedes STAR or compatible equipment is essential to identify the exact cause.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the OM668, OM640 and OM607 engines in the A160 CDI?

acceptedAnswer.text: The OM668 is a 1.7-litre Mercedes-designed diesel used in the W168 A160 CDI (1998-2004), producing 60 hp with a timing chain. The OM640 is a 2.0-litre Mercedes-designed diesel used in the W169 A160 CDI (2004-2012), producing 82 hp with a timing chain. The OM607 is a 1.5-litre Renault K9K-sourced diesel used in the W176 A160 CDI (2013-2015), producing 90 hp with a timing belt.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes-Benz A-Class 160 CDI - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The A160 CDI badge represents the entry-level diesel option across three generations of the Mercedes-Benz A-Class, evolving from the original OM668 1.7-litre in the W168 to the OM640 2.0-litre in the W169, and finally to the Renault-sourced OM607 1.5-litre in the W176 facelift. It has consistently been the most fuel-efficient diesel in the A-Class range.

milestones.description: OM668 DE 17 A (668.941), 1.7L diesel, 60 hp (44 kW) - W168 A160 CDI launch; Mercedes' first common-rail diesel in a compact car; 160 Nm torque
Facelift with revised engine management; power remains 60 hp; emissions improved
OM640 DE 20 LA (640.942), 2.0L diesel, 82 hp (60 kW) - W169 A160 CDI launch; 60 kW output
Facelift with stop/start system; power remains 82 hp
W176 generation launches; A160 CDI initially not available in UK
OM607 D 15 R (607.951), 1.5L diesel, 90 hp (66 kW) - W176 A160 CDI facelift launch; Renault K9K-sourced engine with timing belt
A160 CDI badge discontinued; replaced by A180d

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes-Benz A-Class 160 CDI is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h3: The A160 CDI has been powered by three different diesel engines across its production life - the original OM668 1.7-litre (W168), the OM640 2.0-litre (W169), and the Renault-sourced OM607 1.5-litre (W176). Each has distinct failure patterns. Rebuilt A160 CDI engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: OM668 & OM640 Timing Chain Wear - Why the W168 and W169 A160 CDI Rattles on Cold Start
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz A-Class 160 CDI (OM668.941 and OM640.942, W168 and W169, 1998-2012)
problems.rootCause: Both the OM668 and OM640 use timing chains designed to last the lifetime of the engine, but wear and stretching can occur as the vehicle ages. A loose or stretched timing chain can throw off the engine's timing, leading to poor performance and increased fuel consumption. Owners often notice a rattling sound, particularly when starting the engine.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new chain and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped or engine is badly worn

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical W168 A160 CDI is worth £800-£2,500, while a W169 A160 CDI is worth £1,500-£4,000 depending on condition and mileage. For W168 vehicles, a full engine replacement often exceeds the car's value - a used engine or targeted repair is usually more economical. For W169 vehicles in good condition, a rebuilt OM640 with warranty (£1,500-£2,800) can be a worthwhile investment.
problems.recommendation: If you hear a rattling noise from the engine on cold starts - especially on higher-mileage W168 or W169 models - have the timing system inspected immediately. A preventative chain replacement at a specialist saves thousands compared to waiting for failure. Routine oil changes with high-quality oils can help prolong the timing chain's life.

problems.h4: OM668 & OM640 Injector Seal & Fuel Injection Problems
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz A-Class 160 CDI (OM668.941 and OM640.942, W168 and W169, 1998-2012)
problems.rootCause: Clogged fuel injectors can lead to poor engine performance and increased fuel consumption. Malfunctioning injectors may cause rough idling and misfires. Injector seal failure is also common, causing combustion gas blow-by and poor cold starting.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Remove injectors, replace seals and bolts
repairOptions.longevity: Viable if injectors are not seized

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace all four injectors, fuel system flush
repairOptions.longevity: Required if injectors are seized or damaged

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new injectors and seals
repairOptions.longevity: Only if injector seizure has caused cylinder head damage

problems.recommendation: If you experience poor cold starting, rough idling, or a chuffing noise from the engine bay, have the injector seals inspected. Replacing all four seals at a specialist costs £350-£600 and is far cheaper than the £1,800+ bill for injector replacement if they seize.

problems.h4: OM668 & OM640 Oil Leaks - Ageing Seals and Gaskets
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes-Benz A-Class 160 CDI (OM668.941 and OM640.942, W168 and W169, 1998-2012)
problems.rootCause: Oil leakage is a common issue due to aging seals and gaskets. Heat and friction cause these components to wear out, leading to oil seeping from various points, such as the valve cover gasket, oil pan, and even around the timing cover.

repairOptions.longevity: Viable; prevents oil leaks from top of engine

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine with new seals and gaskets
repairOptions.longevity: Only if oil starvation has caused engine damage

problems.recommendation: Check for oil spots under the car regularly - early detection can prevent more serious engine damage. Regular oil changes with high-quality lubricants can also extend the life of these seals, reducing the likelihood of leaks.
problems.cta: -> Compare oil leak repair and engine replacement prices for your A160 CDI

problems.h4: OM607 Timing Belt Failure - The Renault-Sourced Engine's Critical Weak Point
problems.rootCause: The OM607 is a Renault K9K-sourced engine that uses a timing belt rather than a chain. The belt must be replaced every 80,000-100,000 miles - failure causes piston-to-valve contact and complete engine destruction.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing belt, tensioner, water pump
repairOptions.longevity: Essential maintenance; do not exceed 100k miles

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt engine with new belt and tensioner
repairOptions.longevity: Required if belt has snapped; valves and pistons damaged

problems.recommendation: Unlike chain-driven engines, the OM607's timing belt failure is predictable and preventable. If your OM607-equipped A160 CDI is approaching 80,000 miles or 5 years since the last belt change, replace it immediately. A £350-£650 specialist belt change is far cheaper than a £2,200+ engine replacement.
